description: The definitive list that answers "I want to do X in Python, which tool should I use?"

summary.one_liner: Awesome Python is a curated, categorized list of popular Python frameworks, libraries, and tools, organized by task (e.g. "I want to do X in Python, which tool should I use?").
summary.what_it_does: This is an "awesome" list rather than a software project: it links to third-party Python packages grouped into categories such as AI and ML, Web Development, HTTP and Scraping, Databases, Data and Science, Developer Tools, DevOps, CLI and GUI, Text and Documents, Media, Python Language, Python Toolchain, and Security. Each category has subsections (for example, Web Frameworks splits into Synchronous and Asynchronous) with one-line descriptions per project. Some entries point to other awesome lists for deeper coverage, and some note standard-library modules or licensing caveats. The README is long and was truncated in the provided text, so categories near the end (such as Text Processing onward) were not fully visible. The README also says it is opinionated and that a companion website offers search and filtering.
use_cases: find a Python library for a specific task
compare web frameworks like Flask, Django, and FastAPI
pick a machine learning or deep learning library
choose a database driver or ORM
discover CLI and GUI toolkits for Python
find testing, linting, or debugging tools
notable: Organized by task category with one-line descriptions for each project
Covers AI and agents, LLM serving, and fine-tuning alongside classic Python tooling
Links to related specialized awesome lists (e.g. awesome-flask, awesome-django, awesome-sqlalchemy)
Companion website offers search and filtering
caveats: README is truncated in the provided text, so later categories were not fully reviewed
Includes sponsor slots, which are excluded from this summary
Listed projects are not vetted beyond the list's own opinions; quality and maintenance vary
